purpose: Reference-repository measurements from which lib/thresholds.js bands are derived. Append-only: superseded observations are marked include_in_derivation false with a reason, never deleted.

observations.why_reference: Rebase-and-land trunk workflow with PR-URL trailers; no squash, no merge commits, individual reviewed commits kept intact.

Because this window's production file set was 90.6% vendored deps/ code, duplication_pct was computed both ways: 9.76% (percentage over all 1,113 touched files, includes deps/) and 3.43% (percentage over the 105 non-deps/ files only, re-run with the same jscpd flags). Repeated on a repo with a heavy vendoring practice, this pattern (large deps/ syncs periodically dominating a window) is structural rather than a one-off: a scan of 2026-02-01 to 2026-03-15 found 11 more commits over 1,500 changed lines, several of them deps: syncs (sqlite, simdjson, npm x3, minimatch, ada) or single huge feature/test commits (a 79,262-line 'add node:ffi module' commit, a 87,323-line simdjson vendor bump). Any ~50-commit window of node's mainline has a good chance of containing at least one such commit; this was not cherry-picked to be worse than typical.

window.actual_span: 2026-03-24 to 2026-08-14 (author-date range of the 50 analyzed commits; one long-lived branch, 'cleanup-7-0-barrel', authored starting in March and merged to main much later, pulls the low end of this range back well before the --since committer-date cutoff)

observations.exclusion_reason: TOOL ARTIFACT, not a property of this window: lib/git.js computes each commit's stats with `git show --numstat --format="" <sha>`, which for a two-parent merge diffs against the first parent by default. For a single-commit PR merged via GitHub's 'Merge pull request' button, that reproduces the exact diff of the merge's sole child commit, so the same real-world change is counted twice in the 50-commit sample as if it were two independent commits. In this window 10 of the 50 analyzed commits are such merges, and 6 of them exactly duplicate a sibling commit's (additions, deletions, files_changed) signature -- e.g. 26071400 'Merge pull request #21542' and a5936755 'Deprecate Evented...' both show (1080, 286, 30) -- so 12/50 (24%) of the sample double-counts 6 real changes. This inflates large_commits_pct/sprawling_commits_pct (a large change is flagged large twice) and skews message_quality_pct (the same change is scored once under its real message and once under the generic 'Merge pull request #N from user/branch' message, which is unlikely to pass the message-quality heuristic). Not fixed here per instructions (measurement only); flagged as a new tool defect for repos with true merge-commit history. Superseded: measured at tool_commit 7aedf9c, before two subsequent fixes now at cbfbf9a8 -- (1) cbfbf9a8 scores the full commit message (%B) for message_quality_pct instead of the subject line alone, which changes message_quality_pct for every repository in this dataset, most severely the short-subject/long-body convention used by postgres, curl and git; (2) 055f92ca adds a repo-root-anchored t/ test-directory pattern, which changes test_coverage_rate, test_isolation_rate and uncovered_prod_rate specifically for git/git. All twelve pre-existing observations are retired by this pair of fixes regardless of which specific metrics they touch, since every one was produced by a tool version that undercounted message quality.
observations.notes: DUPLICATE_IGNORE_PATTERNS (**/designs/**) matches nothing in ember.js. duplication_pct (5.12%) scanned 85 production files; ember has no vendored third-party source tree comparable to node's deps/, so no with/without recomputation was needed. test_coverage_rate (10%) and message_quality_pct (16%) look strikingly low for a project this disciplined; given the merge-commit double-counting above, at least part of that is an artifact of the same real commits being scored twice under different messages/shapes rather than ember's actual test or message discipline being this poor -- treat both numbers with suspicion, not just the size metrics.

observations.merge_style_evidence: 128 true two-parent merge commits ('Merge branch 'x/y'') and 0 squash signatures (`\(#[0-9]+\)$`) in 444 commits since 2026-07-01. 441/444 committers are 'Junio C Hamano' (the integrator), consistent with the maintainer-merges-topic-branches model; authors of the underlying commits are individual contributors, preserved with their own names and messages inside each merge.
observations.exclusion_reason: TWO tool defects combine here, both newly found during this calibration round and neither specific to this window: (1) NEW test-file-detection blind spot -- git.git's entire test suite lives under a directory literally named `t/` (e.g. t/t2207-add-resolved.sh, t/helper/test-revision-walking.c), and CONFIG.TEST_FILE_PATTERNS' `(^|\/)tests?\/` pattern requires the literal word 'test' or 'tests' as a path segment, so it never matches `t/`. Every commit's test_files_count was 0 in this run (confirmed directly against local_commit_metrics.json: commits touching t/t1400-update-ref.sh etc. all show test_files_count=0, prod_files_count>0), which is why test_coverage_rate=0.00%, test_isolation_rate=0.00% and uncovered_prod_rate=30.00% -- these numbers describe the pattern's blind spot, not git's actual test discipline (git is one of the most heavily test-covered C projects there is). (2) The same merge-commit double-counting defect documented on ember.js: 36 of 50 analyzed commits are two-parent merges (`git show --numstat` on a merge diffs against first-parent by default), and several exactly duplicate a sibling commit signature, inflating large/sprawling counts. message_quality_pct=0.00% is a separate, softer concern (see notes) but compounds the unreliability of this observation. Superseded: measured at tool_commit 7aedf9c, before two subsequent fixes now at cbfbf9a8 -- (1) cbfbf9a8 scores the full commit message (%B) for message_quality_pct instead of the subject line alone, which changes message_quality_pct for every repository in this dataset, most severely the short-subject/long-body convention used by postgres, curl and git; (2) 055f92ca adds a repo-root-anchored t/ test-directory pattern, which changes test_coverage_rate, test_isolation_rate and uncovered_prod_rate specifically for git/git. All twelve pre-existing observations are retired by this pair of fixes regardless of which specific metrics they touch, since every one was produced by a tool version that undercounted message quality.
observations.notes: message_quality_pct scored 0/50: CONFIG's quality heuristic requires a Conventional-Commits prefix (feat:/fix:/etc, which git.git's 'component: summary' subject style does not use, e.g. 'mailmap: map Elijah Newren's current and previous work addresses' is not conventional-commit-shaped) OR >=10 words in the subject line alone (scoreMessageQuality is only ever given the git-log '%s' subject, never the body). Git's own CONTRIBUTING documentation explicitly asks for a short subject with the explanation in the body -- exactly the style this heuristic scores as low-quality. This is a construct-validity concern with message_quality_pct itself, not a bug in this run, but it means the metric conflates 'long/conventional subject line' with 'well-explained commit,' which will systematically penalize any project (git, and likely postgres, and the Linux-kernel-style C world generally) that puts the explanation in the body instead of the subject. duplication_pct (1.45%) scanned 169 production files; DUPLICATE_IGNORE_PATTERNS (**/designs/**) matches nothing in git.git.
